symptom: `grant access on published rest service M.Svc to M.Role` fails with "published rest service not found: M.Svc" when the service was created with a `folder '…'` clause earlier in the same script, and exec rolls the whole script back; `check -p --references` passes. Without the folder, with a folder that already existed, or with the grant in a second exec it resolves. Same for describe/drop of a scheduled event, task queue, regular expression or consumed REST service created in a new folder — and a re-run `create or modify` of any of the five in the same script silently created a SECOND document of the same name
cause: Exec caches the container hierarchy once (ctx.Cache.hierarchy) and resolves every document's module by walking up from its ContainerID. The CREATE's own existence check built that cache, then resolveFolder → createFolder made the folder, and nothing recorded it: the walk stopped at an unknown folder, GetModuleName returned "", and the name comparison missed. Every other container-changing write (create module, move document, move/drop folder, applyDocumentFolder, rename module) already invalidated the cache; folder creation was the gap. It stayed hidden on most doctypes because their CREATE invalidates the hierarchy afterwards (microflow, page, workflow, enumeration, constant, image collection, OData, …) or their lookup does not use it (menu: GetMenuDocumentByQualifiedName); published REST, consumed REST, scheduled event, task queue and regular expression do neither
file: `mdl/executor/helpers.go` (createFolder now records the folder via ContainerHierarchy.addFolder in hierarchy.go); `cmd_pages_builder.go` (pageBuilder.createFolder delegates to it); guard and tests in `mdl/executor/hierarchy_created_folder_test.go`
insight: Pin the trigger before reading code: three exec variants (no folder / folder pre-existing from a previous exec / grant in a second exec) all passed, so the defect was a per-exec cache going stale on a write, not a folder-scoped lookup — the lookup was already folder-aware. Then audit by DOCTYPE, not by statement: 19 doctypes × create-in-new-folder + lookup, warm and cold cache, split the failures exactly along 'does this CREATE call invalidateHierarchy at the end', which is the tell that the fix belongs in the folder creator rather than in five handlers. Fixture trap that hid it: document_placement_test.go's mock CreateFolder registers the new folder into the cached hierarchy itself — the very bookkeeping production lacked; the new fixture's CreateFolder deliberately does not. The silent duplicate on re-run is the more damaging half and is what a stale existence check always becomes in a CREATE OR MODIFY. check had nothing to predict: its grant-ref validation tracks script-created documents correctly; exec's cache was wrong. Guard: TestFolderCreationHasOneCallSite fails if a second Backend.CreateFolder call site appears in the executor
fix: createFolder records each new folder in the cached hierarchy (addFolder); the page builder's folder creator delegates to it, leaving one call site
